Scales: how data values become colors and sizes

Source: R/mira_scales.R
mira_scales.Rd

A scale turns the values of a mapped attribute into colors or sizes. In ggmira the scale lives in the component that maps the attribute: in mira_node(), mira_intralayer(), mira_interlayer() and mira_layer(), color_by chooses what is colored, and five arguments in the same call choose the colors: color_scale (one color per value, or a gradient), color_palette and color_reverse (which colors), color_limits (the ends of a gradient) and color_values (colors given by hand).

Color

  • color_scale = "categorical" gives each value its own color (MiRA's Dark2 palette); "continuous" a gradient (Viridis, from the column's minimum to its maximum; numeric columns only). Without it, MiRA decides from the data: text gets one color per value; numbers get a gradient when they have more than two values or a name that sounds like a measure (containing weight, abundance, degree, strength, mass, size or value), unless the name marks groups (module, group, cluster, community, partition). mira_options() shows the type MiRA picks for each attribute.

  • color_palette chooses the palette by name (matched without case):

    • categorical: "Dark2" (MiRA's default), "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Paired", "Accent", "Okabe-Ito" (colorblind-safe). Columns with more values than colors reuse them, so two values can share a color (the palettes have 8 to 12 colors).

    • continuous, sequential: "viridis" (MiRA's default), "magma", "cividis" (colorblind-optimized), "Blues", "Greens", "Reds", "Purples", "Oranges", "Greys", "YlOrRd", "YlGnBu".

    • continuous, diverging (two sides of a middle): "RdBu", "RdYlBu", "Spectral", "PiYG", "BrBG", "PuOr".

    A categorical palette gives a categorical scale and a continuous one a gradient, so color_scale is not needed with it. color_reverse = TRUE reverses the palette (light to dark, or the two sides of a diverging one). In MiRA, the legend has the same choices.

  • color_limits = c(min, max) sets the ends of a gradient instead of the data's range, so several plots can share one scale (e.g. 0 to 1 for proportions); values outside take the end colors. With a diverging palette, limits centered on 0 put the middle color at 0. It gives a continuous scale.

  • Palettes and limits need no values, so they also work for the attributes MiRA computes (intra_degree_sum, ...).

  • color_values sets the colors of some values, named by value: c("1" = "red", "3" = "#1f77b4") (numbers need quotes as names). Values not listed keep the palette's color. It gives a categorical scale, so it cannot be combined with color_scale = "continuous".

  • On a bipartite network, mira_node() takes all five per node set: color_scale = c(bird = "continuous"), color_palette = c(bird = "magma"), color_reverse = c(bird = TRUE), color_limits = list(bird = c(0, 10)), color_values = list(plant = c(species = "blue")). They differ between the sets only when the sets are colored by different attributes (one scale per attribute name, below).

  • Two special mappings take colors named by element rather than by value: mira_layer(color_by = "layer_name", color_values = c(L1 = "red")) colors layers one by one, and mira_node(color_by = ".set", color_values = c(bird = "red")) colors the two node sets. These two are not scales: they take color_values only, and color_scale, color_palette, color_reverse and color_limits with them are errors.

One scale per attribute name. MiRA keeps one color scale (type, palette, reversal, limits and colors) per attribute name, used wherever that attribute colors nodes, links or layers (as in MiRA's legends, where changing a color changes it for every element). So when two components color by the same attribute name, their settings are merged: a value that appears in both tables (node module 1 and link module 1) has one color. If the components disagree (a value given two colors, or two scale types), the later one wins, with a warning; a continuous scale cannot be combined with color_values for the same attribute (an error). A color, or a color_by of a different column, drops that component's earlier color_values and color_scale.

Size

mira_node(size_by = ) sizes nodes by a numeric attribute, scaled by MiRA from the smallest to the largest value; size sets the base size (and the only size, without size_by). Link width always follows the weight column, which is why weight cannot color links. A size range from R is planned.

See also

mira() for how components combine.

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

# Colors of some values; the others keep MiRA's palette
p + mira_node(color_by = "verification_level",
              color_values = c(species = "#1f77b4", genus = "orange"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# The same numeric attribute as a gradient, or one color per value
p + mira_node(color_by = "intra_degree_sum", color_scale = "continuous")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_node(color_by = "intra_degree_sum", color_scale = "categorical")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# A palette, reversed; a gradient with fixed ends
p + mira_node(color_by = "verification_level", color_palette = "Okabe-Ito")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_node(color_by = "intra_degree_sum", color_palette = "magma", color_reverse = TRUE)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_node(color_by = "intra_degree_sum", color_palette = "cividis", color_limits = c(0, 30))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_intralayer(color_by = "type", color_palette = "Set1")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Per node set
p + mira_node(color_by = c(bird = "intra_degree_sum", plant = "verification_level"),
              color_scale = c(bird = "continuous"),
              color_values = list(plant = c(species = "blue")))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# One color per layer; the colors of the two node sets
p + mira_layer(color_by = "layer_name", color_values = c(layer_1 = "orange"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
p + mira_node(color_by = ".set", color_values = c(bird = "red", plant = "green"))
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Size by an attribute, from a base size
p + mira_node(size_by = "intra_degree_sum", size = 6)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
